newsitem.title: UK: S&P assigns ratings to five Slovakian banks.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns ratings to five Slovakian banks.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had assigned public information (pi) ratings to five Slovakian banks as part of its expanded bank ratings coverage.
"Three of the ratings are in the BBpi category and two in the Bpi category," S&P said in a statement.

It said the "pi" following the rating indicates that Standard & Poor's employed analytical procedures which parallel its traditional credit ratings, but differ in that they are based on public disclosure of bank information and other sources.
S&P said that the three banks rated BBpi were Vseobecna Uverova Banka which is the largest commercial bank, Tatra Banka, a subsidiary of RZB, and Slovenska Sporitelna, the largest savings bank.
It added that Bpi ratings have been assigned to Polnobanka, a medium sized rapidly growing bank; and Investicna a Razvojova Banka, which serves large, strategically important infrastructure projects.
"Despite substantial state support for the three largest banks, bank creditworthiness in Slovakia is still weak when judged by international standards," S&P said.

"Compared with other countries in the region, there is relatively little improvement in the banks' credit quality, and commercial lending based on sound credit criteria has yet to show tangible qualitative results," it said.
It said the sector was struggling with a number of problems which result in its lagging behind other Vishegrad countries.
"Constant postponement of the privatization process has discouraged foreign investors, whose involvement is of paramount importance," it said.

S&P said it was also concerned about substantial levels of bad debts in bank portfolios and the potential for a number of corporate bankruptcies. "Inadequate risk assessment and failure to create appropriate risk reserves can have serious implications for a bank's financial stability," it saidm'
